summary: Guest threads in the game's forms (specs/work_list.json), sequenced by events so every run prints the same rows. CreateThread: a handle (a multiple of 4), a new id, the last error left; the new thread runs each module's TLS callback then DllMain with DLL_THREAD_ATTACH, then its routine with the last error 187, empty TLS slots and its own static TLS (the template's 41), and at its end the same with DLL_THREAD_DETACH; created suspended, none of it until resumed. GetExitCodeThread: 259 while it runs, then its return or ExitThread's code. SuspendThread and ResumeThread answer the previous count; a suspended thread runs no instruction; on an ended thread SuspendThread fails with 5 and ResumeThread answers 0. GetThreadContext: TRUE, ContextFlags as asked, RIP in the image, RSP in the thread's stack, CS 0x33, SS 0x2B. Priorities -2 and 0 read back, 100 is error 87; the description calls answer 0x10000000; SleepEx answers 0; AppPolicyGetThreadInitializationType gives policy 0.

open_questions: The order of the TLS callbacks and DllMain calls between modules is not in the rows (the probe has one DLL); w2m calls each DLL's in load order, the program's TLS callbacks last.
SwitchToThread's answer depends on what else is ready on the CPU; the row keeps only that it is TRUE or FALSE.

A thread's stack in w2m is all committed above StackLimit with no guard pages, where Windows commits on demand behind a guard page; threads.c and VirtualQuery show the difference only to code that probes another thread's stack pages.
